evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immunity and capacity also limit what a lot can do. points.requirement: Particle or fluorescent-lipid signal does not by itself establish intact RNA in the cytosol, encoded protein or useful function.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where particles go depends on formulation and route. In female BALB/c mice given luciferase-mRNA LNPs by intramuscular, subcutaneous or intravenous injection, some intramuscular particles reached the liver and spleen, smaller particles more than larger ones, bigger particles tended to stay at the injection site, and liver expression was the most prominent; exposure and expression were not linearly related (Di and colleagues). Mouse distribution is not another product's distribution in people, and local injection does not establish local delivery. Readouts answer different questions: particle size, RNA integrity and encapsulated fraction describe the product; a labelled lipid or labelled RNA shows where a label went, not that intact RNA arrived or was released; and protein per identified live cell shows expression. In the mouse study a lipid label (DiR or deuterium-labelled cholesterol) and luciferase activity were measured separately and did not track each other linearly, and every figure needs its denominator (all cells, live cells or expressing cells). Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. Message and effect also run on separate clocks: in cultured mouse T cells CAR expression from LNP mRNA peaked at 24 hours and fell over the next days (Rurik and colleagues), and the same RNA in particles of different size or by a different route distributed differently, so the same RNA is not the same product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A typical RNA-delivery lipid nanoparticle combines an ionisable lipid, a phospholipid, cholesterol and a polyethylene glycol lipid around the RNA; the proportions, lipid identities and preparation change behaviour, so the label LNP alone does not name a product. evidence.supportingExcerpt: In an invented comparison using 100 identified live cells per formulation at the same measurement time, A shows uptake in 70 cells and encoded protein in 10; B shows uptake in 40 and protein in 25. Uptake is therefore 70 versus 40 per cent, while protein expression is 10 versus 25 per cent on the same live-cell denominator. These separate counts do not show which cells had both signals, the fraction of intact RNA that escaped, the amount of protein per cell or a biological effect. Name the cargo, cell population, assay, timing and controls before comparing formulations; a brighter carrier signal alone does not establish usable RNA delivery.
